claim: Context window sizes across major models as of early 2026: GPT-4 8K-variant at 8,192 tokens, GPT-4o at 128,000 tokens, Claude 3.5 Sonnet at 200,000 tokens, Claude Sonnet 4 at 1,000,000 tokens, Gemini 1.5 Flash at 1,000,000 tokens, Gemini 1.5 Pro up to 2,000,000 tokens, and Llama 3.1 at 128,000 tokens.
stance_target: comparative context-window capacity of production LLMs
quoted_support: Here's what current context windows look like across major models... Claude Sonnet 4 | 1,000,000 tokens... Gemini 1.5 Pro | up to 2,000,000 tokens

claim: Self-attention has O(n^2) computational complexity: a 10,000-token context requires about 100 million pairwise comparisons, while a 100,000-token context requires about 10 billion.
stance_target: raw context-window size scaling faces a hard quadratic computational ceiling, motivating context engineering over brute-force expansion
quoted_support: Transformers need to compare every token to every other token. Double your context and you quadruple the work. A 10K token context needs 100 million comparisons. A 100K token context needs 10 billion.

claim: Accuracy degrades sharply for most long-context LLMs beyond roughly 32,000 tokens due to the 'lost-in-the-middle' effect, with even top performers like GPT-4o showing significant accuracy loss at longer context lengths.
stance_target: bigger context windows alone reliably improve agent task performance
scope_conditions: long-context LLM benchmarks referenced generally, as of 2026
quoted_support: In practice, most long-context models show sharp performance drops past 32K tokens. Even top performers like GPT-4o lose significant accuracy at longer contexts. Don't trust the spec sheet: benchmark your actual use case at your target context length.

claim: KV-cache CPU-GPU data transfer overhead typically consumes 70-90% of inference time, and switching KV-cache precision from f16 to q8_0 or q4_0 quantization cuts cache memory usage by approximately 50%.
stance_target: memory-management engineering (quantization, caching) is necessary infrastructure for cost-efficient agent context handling
scope_conditions: LLM inference infrastructure, general, as of 2026
quoted_support: Quantization (switching from f16 to q8_0 or q4_0 cuts cache usage by ~50%)... introduces CPU-GPU data transfer overhead that typically consumes 70-90% of inference time.

claim: Production LLM systems should combine semantic caching, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and dual-layer agent memory (short-term conversational plus long-term vector-indexed) rather than relying on ever-larger context windows alone, because RAG accuracy stays stable as a corpus scales while long-context recall degrades.
stance_target: context engineering infrastructure (RAG + caching + memory) outperforms brute-force context-window scaling for cost and reliability
quoted_support: RAG retrieves only relevant document sections rather than stuffing everything into the context window. This approach maintains stable accuracy as your document corpus grows, while long-context models tend to degrade past tens of thousands of tokens.
